Name: Lists
Summary: Short ordered lists such as an FAQ, services, features or steps: entries with a title, Markdown text, an optional image and an optional link.
Guide:
One instance is one list, so a site with an FAQ and a list of services adds two instances. Entries have no pages of their own: a list is shown whole, on the page it is placed on or anywhere else through a template function.

Add it to the site

app.Use(
    lists.Module("faq", "FAQ"),
    lists.Module("services", "Services"),
)

The key (faq) is the list's name in URLs and templates and must be unique on the site. The title (FAQ) is what editors see in the admin navigation and the page editor.

Place it on a page

In the admin, open a page and choose the list under Shows on this page. With the page at /faq:

Address Template Shows
/faq faq/list.gohtml the published entries, in the order set in the admin

Other addresses below the page get the site's 404 page. Templates are looked up by instance key first, then by module type, so lists/list.gohtml serves every list that has no design of its own; .Key tells the lists apart inside a shared template. Generate a starting point with every field of the data:

task templates -- faq

A minimal FAQ:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/lists.ListView */}}
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>

{{range .Entries}}
    <article id="{{.ID}}">
        {{with .ImageURL}}<img src="{{image . "120x120 crop"}}" width="120" height="120" alt="">{{end}}
        <h2>{{.Title}}</h2>
        {{.Body}}
        {{with .Link}}<a href="{{.}}">Read more</a>{{end}}
    </article>
{{end}}

Title is the published title of the page the list is placed on. Body is the rendered Markdown, with media from the library already resolved. Link is a template.URL, so tel: links work in href. ImageURL is the image as pages show it, at most 1600 pixels wide, with ImageSrcset, ImageWidth and ImageHeight for an img tag of that size and ImageOriginalURL for the uploaded file; given ImageURL, image makes the square copy above from the uploaded image (see Media and images). Keep id="{{.ID}}" on each entry, as the generated starting point does: site search results link to #<id> on the list's page, and the ID never changes.

An entry appears in each language it has a title for.

Show a list anywhere

The entries template function returns the published entries of a list in the current language, in their order. The list does not need to be placed on a page for this.

<section>
    <h2>Frequently asked</h2>
    {{range entries "faq"}}
        <h3>{{.Title}}</h3>
        {{.Body}}
    {{end}}
    <a href="{{moduleURL "faq"}}">All questions</a>
</section>

Content API

While the site's content API is on (Config.API), /api/v1/<key>/entries serves the published entries as JSON, in the language of ?locale=, or the site's default language without it. With the list faq:

Endpoint Route name Answers with
/api/v1/faq/entries api.faq.entries The published entries, in the editors' order, as a list
/api/v1/faq/entries/{id} api.faq.entry One entry

Entries have no page of their own, so the list gives each entry whole: its id, title and body_html, its image as an image object, null without one, its link, url, api_url and updated_at. link is the entry's link as a visitor follows it from the list's page: a path of the site made absolute, an anchor on the list's page, and other addresses, such as mailto: links, as they are; null without a link. url is the entry on the list's page, such as https://example.com/en/faq#<id>, and null while the list is on no page.

/entries/{id} sends a Last-Modified: the latest change of the entry, of the page the instance is on and of the entry's media, its image and those in its text. An entry with an image that was deleted gets none, and so does every entry while the instance is on no page; the lists get none either; see Caching.

Editing

Each list has its own section in the admin (/admin/faq; /admin is the default admin path) with its entries.

  • An entry has an optional image from the media library and an optional link, shared by all languages, and per language a title and Markdown text.
  • A link is a path on the site (/contact), an anchor (#opening-hours), or a web, mailto: or tel: address.
  • Entries have no drafts or revisions: saving changes the entry at once, also when it is published. New entries start unpublished at the end of the list. Publish and Unpublish show or hide an entry; publishing needs a title in the site's default language.
  • The move buttons on the overview set the order of the entries on the site.
  • Move to trash moves an entry to the trash, where it can be restored or deleted for good.

Editors' rights are set per list in the groups' permission matrix.

Published entries appear in the site search by title and text once the list is placed on a page.

Links to addresses on the site in the text and links of published entries count for Links to a page: the editor of a page lists the entries that link to it, and Pages › Broken links lists their links that lead nowhere.

From Go

lists.Of(app, "faq") returns the list once the app has started:

faq := lists.Of(app, "faq")

entries, err := faq.Entries(ctx, "en")

Store() gives write access for imports and seed data, through the same rules the admin uses:

store := faq.Store()

entry, err := store.Save(ctx, content.Draft[lists.Fields, lists.Text]{
    Fields: lists.Fields{
        Link: "/contact",
    },
    Translations: []content.Translation[lists.Text]{
        {
            Locale: "en",
            Text: lists.Text{
                Title: "Do you deliver?",
                Body:  "Within the city, yes. [Ask us](/contact) about other places.",
            },
        },
    },
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

err = store.Publish(ctx, entry.ID, "", "en")

Related modules

  • People suits a team, with a page and contact details per person.
  • Testimonials keeps quotes from customers.
  • Gallery shows albums of images.

Funcs.Name: entries
Funcs.Doc: entries returns the published entries of a list, for example {{range entries "faq"}} on any page.

Templates.Name: list

Fields.Name: Key
Fields.Doc: Key is the list's instance key, for example "faq", so one template can show several lists differently.

Fields.Name: Title
Fields.Doc: Title is the title of the page the list is mounted on.

Fields.Name: ImageURL
Fields.Doc: ImageURL is the entry's image as pages show it, at most media.ImageWidth wide (see frontend.Frontend.Image); ImageSrcset lists smaller copies for a srcset attribute, ImageWidth and ImageHeight are the size of ImageURL and ImageOriginalURL is the uploaded file, for downloads. All are empty when the entry has no image.

Fields.Name: Link
Fields.Doc: Link is empty when not set. It is a template.URL because the store only accepts paths, anchors and http(s), mailto: and tel: addresses, so templates can use it in href without html/template replacing tel: links with #ZgotmplZ.

SQL.Name: postgres
SQL.SQL:
-- One row per list entry; the instance is the list (see content.Collection).
CREATE TABLE wt_lists_entry (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by UUID,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by UUID,
    image_id   UUID,
    link_url   VARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE INDEX wt_lists_entry_instance ON wt_lists_entry (instance, position);

CREATE TABLE wt_lists_entry_translation (
    item_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES wt_lists_entry (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    locale  VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    title   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    body    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale)
);

SQL.Name: mysql
SQL.SQL:
-- One row per list entry; the instance is the list (see content.Collection).
CREATE TABLE wt_lists_entry (
    id         VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    image_id   VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    link_url   VARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    INDEX wt_lists_entry_instance (instance, position)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE wt_lists_entry_translation (
    item_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    locale  VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    title   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    body    MEDIUMTEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES wt_lists_entry (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

Types.Name: APIEntry
Types.Doc: APIEntry is a published entry in the content API (see package api), at /api/v1/<key>/entries/{id} and in the list of /api/v1/<key>/entries. Entries have no page of their own: the list's page shows them whole, so the list has their text too.
